overview: Anchisaurus was a small early sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic of northeastern North America. It lived before the gigantic sauropods, at a stage when sauropodomorphs were still relatively light-bodied animals that could move actively on land.

The genus has a tangled naming history, replacing earlier names that were already occupied. PBDB records it from the Portland / Agawam unit in Connecticut and Massachusetts, making it part of the early Jurassic rift-basin dinosaur record of eastern North America.

articles.title: Why it matters
articles.body: Anchisaurus captures sauropodomorphs before the full sauropod body plan: still small, active and close to the evolutionary transition toward giant quadrupedal herbivores.

articles.title: Naming history
articles.body: Its history includes replacement names and taxonomic housekeeping, a reminder that early North American dinosaur nomenclature was often unstable.

record.description: Anchisaurus polyzelus was a small early sauropodomorph from the Portland Formation of Connecticut and Massachusetts. Its anatomy is based on several incomplete skeletons, including the neotype YPM 1883; Ammosaurus is a junior synonym.
facts: The accepted species spelling is polyzelus, not polyzelous.
The Manchester quarry material formerly named Ammosaurus major belongs to Anchisaurus in the modern revision.

review.ageReviewNote: The Portland Formation material is Early Jurassic, broadly Hettangian-Sinemurian.
